INTERACTIVE PROOF - ELEMENTARY NUMBER THEORY

Why Odd Numbers Build Perfect Squares

THEOREM

For every natural number n, the sum of the first n odd numbers is n2: 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n - 1) = n2.

PROOF BY INDUCTION

Write Sn for 1 + 3 + ... + (2n - 1). For n = 0, the sum is empty, so S0 = 0 = 02. Now assume Sn = n2. The next odd number is 2n + 1, hence

Sn+1 = Sn + (2n + 1) = n2 + 2n + 1 = (n + 1)2.

Therefore the identity holds for n + 1, and induction proves it for every natural number n.

WHY THE ALGEBRA MATCHES THE PICTURE

To enlarge an n by n square, attach one column of n cells and one row of n + 1 cells. The new L-shaped border contains 2n + 1 cells - exactly the next odd number. The equation (n + 1)2 - n2 = 2n + 1 is the same growth step written algebraically.

FORMALIZATION NOTE

Lean defines oddSum recursively: oddSum 0 = 0 and oddSum (n + 1) = oddSum n + (2 * n + 1). The theorem follows the same induction as the paper; simplification expands the successor square and closes the arithmetic step.
